findings.title: Concurrent goroutines write shared `err` and `totalBatchesIndexed` during startup indexing
findings.body: Inside `group.Go(func() error {...})`, the closure assigns to the outer `err` variable (`_, _, err = s.build(...)`) and increments the outer `totalBatchesIndexed` without synchronization. With `initWorkers` > 1 these run concurrently, which is a data race (flagged by `-race`) and can return the wrong error or lose the count. The closure should use a local `err :=` and an atomic counter.

findings.title: Removing the BuildIndex lock allows duplicate concurrent builds for the same key
findings.body: The whole `BuildIndex` used to be serialized by `cacheMu`. The lock now only guards the final map write, so two concurrent `getOrCreateIndex` calls for the same namespace/resource (possible from Search and watch events, which both call `build` when `GetIndex` returns nil) will both build. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold) both call `bleve.New(dir, ...)` on the same directory, and one will fail or corrupt the other. The second build also overwrites the cache entry, leaking the first index. Per-key locking (singleflight or a per-key mutex) is needed, not an unlocked build.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the cache map without holding the lock
findings.body: `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` with no `cacheMu` read lock, while `BuildIndex` writes to the same map under the write lock and `GetIndex` reads it under RLock. Concurrent map iteration and insertion is a fatal runtime error in Go. It is now also called from `searchSupport.init` logging, and `search.init` can run while Search requests are building indexes. It should take `cacheMu.RLock()`.

findings.title: Initialization now runs in the constructor and blocks/fails NewResourceServer
findings.body: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)`, which runs lifecycle hooks, the full search index build for all namespaces above InitMinCount, and starts the watcher. Callers now get a slow constructor, and any Init failure (including a lifecycle hook that expects the server to be fully constructed or registered) makes the constructor return an error rather than letting the caller handle it. Callers must be audited for whether they can tolerate a long blocking constructor and whether lifecycle hooks depend on the returned server being usable, as the PR asks.

findings.title: Event broadcaster now starts after the index build, so writes during the build are missed
findings.body: The order in `Init` was changed so `initWatcher()` runs after `search.init(ctx)`. Any write events that occur while the (now potentially long) index build runs are not buffered by the broadcaster, so Watch clients subscribed through the broadcaster silently miss those events. Previously the watcher was started first to buffer them. The reordering needs justification or the watcher should be started before the build.

findings.title: Init errors from search build are only logged and the server is left in a half-initialized state on Stop
findings.body: When `search.init` fails, `initErr` is set and the constructor returns an error, but the search goroutines and lifecycle started earlier (`lifecycle.Init`) are never torn down because `NewResourceServer` returns `nil, err` without calling `Stop`/`cancel`. The background context created in the constructor leaks.

findings.title: Postgres integration test is now skipped unconditionally
findings.body: The new skip for `postgres` disables the only integration test covering the storage server target for that database, without any tracking issue beyond a TODO. The change is unrelated to the PR's stated goals and reduces coverage of the lazy-to-eager init change for postgres.
